alex: Kicking off a replay run to validate kernel selection + KV-cache behavior against prod traces. Goal: apples-to-apples parity (response hashes + token-level diffs), latency within 5% of prod, determinism with fixed seed. Need an anonymized sample and a pinned batching config for the run. Anyone can review the sampling strategy?

priya: How big are we thinking for the sample? naive 100k might be too heavy for dev GPUs. I'd do stratified sampling by seq_len and customer cohort (web/mobile) to preserve distribution. For anonymization: hash user_id with a salt, strip any free-text user prompts > 200 chars, and remove metadata fields that look like emails/phones. Is that OK for compliance?

alex: Yes to stratified. Target sample = 10k requests with roughly the same seq_len distribution as prod p95. Anon plan sounds right. Will also drop attachments. Command I'm going to run locally:
```
replay-harness \
  --input s3://redwood/traces/2026-03-16/* \
  --sample 10000 \
  --stratify seq_len,cohort \
  --anon-hash-salt redwood-prod-salt-v2 \
  --anon-truncate 200 \
  --seed 42 \
  --out s3://redwood-playground/anons/samples/2026-03-18/sample-10k-seqstrata.jsonl
```
(Simplified)

replay-bot: Started replay job r-job-20260318-001 — logs: https://ci.internal/replay/r-job-20260318-001 · ETA ~35m

marco: Quick note: KV cache warmup matters a lot. If we just replay cold, kernel selection might differ (kernel probe/tiling changes). We should run a two-stage harness: 1) prewarm window of ~5k tokens per model shard to populate KV and measure steady-state; 2) kernel-probe stage that logs chosen kernels per op. Also capture per-request batch_size histogram (continuous batching causes dynamic batches). Example env override: 
```
export KV_WARMUP_TOKENS=5000
export KERNEL_PROBE=1  # forces kernel selection logging
export BATCHING_CONFIG='{"max_delay_ms":10,"max_batch_tokens":4096}'
```

sasha: Also callout: last perf regression (PR #3421) silently moved the continuous batching threshold from 8 -> 16 tokens which changed tail latency. For apples-to-apples, pin batching config in the harness and capture the per-step batching histogram + token throughput percentiles. We should also snapshot the runtime kernel binary hash and GPU driver version for reproducibility.

alex: Good catches. Add these to run checklist: anonymized sample path, stratified seed, KV prewarm tokens, kernel probe enabled, pinned batching config, runtime & driver hashes. For parity checks we'll compute: top-1 response SHA256, token-level Levenshtein distance, and a quick log-probability diff if available. Priya — can you run the anon pipeline and push the sample to the s3 path above? If yes I'll launch the harness with the pinned config and report back with a short perf diff table. :thumbsup:

priya: Done — sample uploaded: s3://redwood-playground/anons/samples/2026-03-18/sample-10k-seqstrata.jsonl. I left a small manifest next to it with stratification buckets and the salt fingerprint. Manifest: s3://redwood-playground/anons/samples/2026-03-18/manifest.json

devops-bot: Replay run r-job-20260318-001 updated: prewarm completed, kernel-probe logs collected (link: https://ci.internal/replay/r-job-20260318-001/logs).

alex: I'll pull logs, compute the parity table (response-hash match %, median latency delta, 99th tail delta, avg tokens/sec) and post results here in ~1h. If we see >2% unmatched responses or big token-level diffs, we escalate to eng-runtime for deeper kernel/kv investigation.

sasha: If you hit non-deterministic outputs, rerun with fixed seed + pinned scheduler and attach the minimal failing trace. We can add a small harness mode that reruns only failing traces with exhaustive kernel selection logging.

marco: Agreed. Also let's ensure the results include per-cohort breakdown — mobile vs web had different batching profiles last time.

alex: noted — reporting will include cohort breakdowns. Thanks all, will share the perf + parity summary when ready.
